title: PM Modi Inaugurates India's First Greenfield Refinery-Petrochemical Hub in Rajasthan
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated India's first Greenfield refinery and petrochemical hub in Rajasthan on July 4, 2026. The project is a significant addition to India's energy infrastructure, aimed at reducing import dependency and boosting domestic petrochemical production. Modi also inaugurated the new terminal at Jodhpur Airport during the same visit to Rajasthan. He stated that India navigated one of the biggest global energy crises by sourcing energy from over 40 countries, averting a fuel crisis with little burden on citizens.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Energy Security and Infrastructure); tests knowledge of India's refinery capacity, energy policy, and the government's push for energy self-reliance.
key_facts: India's first Greenfield refinery-petrochemical hub inaugurated in Rajasthan
India sourced energy from over 40 countries to avert fuel crisis
Jodhpur Airport new terminal also inaugurated by PM Modi
Part of India's broader energy security and infrastructure push

title: PM Modi Inaugurates Rs 7,600 Crore Semiconductor Plant in Gujarat's Sanand
summary: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated a semiconductor manufacturing plant worth Rs 7,600 crore in Sanand, Gujarat on July 4, 2026. The plant is a major milestone under India's semiconductor mission, aimed at building domestic chip manufacturing capability and reducing dependence on imports. Sanand is emerging as a key hub for electronics and semiconductor manufacturing in India. The investment aligns with the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).
exam_angle: Directly relevant to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech and Economy); tests knowledge of India Semiconductor Mission, Make in India, and critical technology supply chains.
key_facts: Investment: Rs 7,600 crore
Location: Sanand, Gujarat
Inaugurated by PM Modi on July 4, 2026
Part of India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) under MeitY

title: Parliament Monsoon Session 2026 Scheduled from July 20 to August 13
summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the Parliament's Monsoon Session 2026 will commence on July 20 and continue till August 13. Reports indicate the Modi government is eyeing Constitutional amendments during this session. The Lok Sabha Speaker is expected to take decisions on pending anti-defection cases during the session. The session will be closely watched for legislative business including potential amendments.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 2 (Polity); connects to Parliamentary procedures, Constitutional amendment process (Articles 368), and the anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule).
key_facts: Monsoon Session 2026: July 20 to August 13
Announced by Minister Kiren Rijiju
Government eyeing Constitutional amendments
Lok Sabha Speaker to decide on anti-defection cases

title: India-UK Free Trade Agreement: Government Notifies Customs Tariff and Rules of Origin
summary: The Government of India has notified customs tariff rules for the India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA), clearing the way for its rollout from July 15, 2026. The notification includes rules for determination of origin of goods, specifying that no tariff benefits will accrue to repackaged goods. The India-UK FTA is one of the most significant trade deals India has concluded in recent years. India's top three ministers headed to Brussels on a trade mission, with Commerce Minister Goyal also providing updates on FTA progress with Canada, Israel, and Peru.
exam_angle: Critical for GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy); tests knowledge of FTA frameworks, Rules of Origin, and India's trade diplomacy.
key_facts: India-UK FTA customs tariff rules notified
Rollout date: July 15, 2026
Rules of Origin notified: no benefits for repackaged goods
India also in FTA talks with Canada, Israel, and Peru

title: Government Sends Takedown Notice to Telegram Over Piracy and Illegal Content
summary: The Central Government issued a formal notice to messaging platform Telegram with a 15-day deadline to take immediate action against pirated films, OTT content, and other illegal material being circulated on the platform. This is part of India's enforcement action under the Information Technology Act and copyright laws. The move underscores the government's ongoing crackdown on digital piracy and misuse of social media/messaging platforms. Telegram has previously faced regulatory scrutiny in multiple countries.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (Governance) and GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech); connects to IT Act provisions, intermediary liability rules, and digital rights enforcement.
key_facts: Notice issued to Telegram by Government of India
15-day deadline given for compliance
Action sought against pirated films and OTT content
Enforcement under Information Technology Act and copyright law

title: Centre Allows Four China-Linked Firms to Participate in Critical Power Sector Tenders
summary: The Central Government has opened critical power sector bids to four China-linked firms, a decision that has drawn opposition from the Congress party. The move comes amid the broader normalization of India-China economic ties following diplomatic engagement post-Galwan. India's envoy to China also stated that more Chinese investment would be good for the wider bilateral relationship. The decision is significant given India's earlier restrictions on Chinese companies in sensitive sectors post-2020.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy); connects to India-China relations, FDI policy in critical infrastructure, and national security concerns around Chinese investments.
key_facts: Four China-linked firms allowed into Indian power sector tenders
Decision criticized by Opposition (Congress)
India's envoy to China: more Chinese investment beneficial for bilateral ties
Reversal of post-2020 restrictions on Chinese firms in sensitive sectors

title: India's Ethanol Blending Programme: Government Busts Myths on E20 Petrol Amid Industry Debate
summary: The Government of India issued clarifications busting 10 myths around E20 petrol (20% ethanol blending), addressing concerns about engine damage and excess water usage. India's auto industry defended the ethanol fuel mandate, stating it was implemented through a scientific and phased approach, and that E20 causes no engine damage though mileage may marginally drop. India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) targets 20% blending by 2025-26 as part of energy security and reducing crude oil import dependency. PM Modi also cited the EBP as part of India averting the global energy crisis.
exam_angle: Important for GS Paper 3 (Environment and Economy); tests knowledge of India's Ethanol Blending Programme, biofuel policy, and energy security measures.
key_facts: E20 = 20% ethanol blended petrol
Government busted 10 myths on E20; no engine damage confirmed
Ethanol Blending Programme target: 20% blending by 2025-26
EBP aimed at reducing crude oil imports and supporting farmers (sugarcane)

title: Centre Lifts Restrictions on Natural Gas Supplies as Middle East Tensions Ease
summary: The Central Government has lifted curbs on natural gas supplies as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East showed signs of easing. This move is expected to stabilize domestic gas availability and moderate prices for industrial and household consumers. Natural gas supply restrictions had been imposed earlier in response to global supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict. The decision is part of India's broader energy management strategy to ensure supply security.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy/Energy); tests understanding of India's natural gas policy, LNG imports, and the impact of global geopolitics on India's energy security.
key_facts: Centre lifts curbs on natural gas supplies
Reason: easing of Middle East geopolitical tensions
Move aimed at stabilizing domestic gas prices and availability
Connects to India's dependence on LNG imports from Middle East

title: Supreme Court SIR Verdict: 23 Opposition Parties Write to Chief Justice of India
summary: Twenty-three opposition parties have written to the Chief Justice of India (CJI) regarding the Supreme Court's verdict on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The SIR process, conducted by the Election Commission, has raised concerns about its implications for citizenship and voting rights. The Supreme Court's verdict on SIR has sparked a national debate on the definition of citizenship versus voter eligibility. The opposition argues the process may disenfranchise eligible voters.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 2 (Polity); connects to Election Commission's role, electoral rolls, citizenship rights (Article 326), and the right to vote as a constitutional right.
key_facts: 23 opposition parties wrote to CJI over Supreme Court SIR verdict
SIR = Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls by Election Commission
Concerns raised about disenfranchisement and citizenship definitions
Connects to Article 326 (right to vote) and Election Commission's powers

title: Security Forces Kill 2 Terrorists in Anti-Terror Operation in J&K's Shopian
summary: Security forces launched a major anti-terror operation (CASO – Cordon and Search Operation) in Shopian district of Jammu & Kashmir on July 4, 2026, resulting in the killing of two terrorists. Shopian district in south Kashmir has historically been a militant hotspot. The operation is part of ongoing counter-insurgency efforts in the Kashmir Valley following the Pahalgam attack earlier in 2026. Security forces continue to intensify operations in the region.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Internal Security); tests knowledge of counter-insurgency operations in J&K, security forces' structure, and the strategic importance of Shopian.
key_facts: 2 terrorists killed in Shopian, J&K
CASO (Cordon and Search Operation) conducted by security forces
Shopian is in south Kashmir, historically a militant-affected district
Part of ongoing counter-insurgency operations post-Pahalgam attack

title: China Launches Coast Guard Patrols East of Taiwan Amid International Criticism
summary: China's coast guard has commenced patrol operations in waters east of Taiwan, which Beijing describes as 'routine law enforcement patrols.' The move has drawn international pushback, with critics viewing it as an escalation of China's assertiveness around Taiwan. The patrols east of Taiwan are significant as they extend China's presence beyond the Taiwan Strait into the Pacific. This development adds to regional tensions in the Indo-Pacific and has implications for India's strategic partnerships.
exam_angle: Important for GS Paper 2 (IR); connects to the Taiwan Strait issue, China's maritime assertiveness, UNCLOS, and India's Indo-Pacific strategy.
key_facts: China launched coast guard patrols east of Taiwan Island
Beijing terms it 'routine law enforcement patrols'
Draws international criticism and pushback
Significant escalation in Indo-Pacific maritime tensions

title: Germany Expresses Concern Over Reports of China Training Russian Troops
summary: Germany has described as 'deeply disturbing' reports that China is training Russian military troops, a development that would mark a significant deepening of China-Russia military cooperation. The reports come amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, where Western nations have been concerned about Chinese support for Russia. If confirmed, such training would represent a major shift in the China-Russia strategic relationship and would have significant implications for NATO and global security architecture. Russia also warned Ukraine that its attacks 'will not go unanswered.'
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR); connects to China-Russia relations, NATO-Russia conflict dynamics, and India's strategic balancing between Russia and the West.
key_facts: Germany called reports of China training Russian troops 'deeply disturbing'
Concerns raised amid ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict
Would mark deepening of China-Russia military cooperation
Russia warned Ukraine attacks 'will not go unanswered'

title: US Department of Justice Drops Charges Against Adani Group, Says Case 'Should Never Have Been Brought'
summary: The United States Department of Justice (DoJ) has formally dropped charges against the Adani Group, stating the case 'should never have been brought' and that 'not a single penny was lost.' The DoJ also stated that 'courts cannot second-guess prosecutors' in explaining the decision. The Adani Group had been charged with alleged bribery in a US indictment filed in November 2024 related to solar energy contracts. The dropping of charges is a significant development for Adani Group's global business operations and investor sentiment.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Economy) and GS Paper 2 (IR); connects to India-US economic relations, corporate governance, and the functioning of US judicial/prosecutorial systems.
key_facts: US DoJ dropped charges against Adani Group
DoJ statement: case 'should never have been brought'
DoJ: 'not a single penny was lost'
Original charges (Nov 2024) related to alleged bribery in solar energy contracts

title: India's Top Ministers Head to Brussels for Trade Mission; FTA Updates on Canada, Israel, Peru
summary: India's top three cabinet ministers embarked on a trade mission to Brussels, Belgium, signaling active engagement with the European Union on trade and economic cooperation. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal provided updates on the status of Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations with Canada, Israel, and Peru. The Brussels visit is significant as India and the EU are engaged in ongoing FTA negotiations. India's multi-front trade diplomacy reflects its effort to diversify export destinations and reduce tariff barriers.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy); tests knowledge of India's FTA strategy, India-EU trade relations, and multilateral economic diplomacy.
key_facts: India's top 3 ministers on trade mission to Brussels (EU)
Commerce Minister Goyal updated on FTA talks with Canada, Israel, Peru
India-EU FTA negotiations ongoing
Part of India's broader multi-front trade diplomacy strategy

title: Health Groups Demand Overhaul of India's National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM)
summary: Health advocacy groups have demanded a comprehensive overhaul of India's National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM), citing outdated inclusions and omissions of newer critical drugs. The NLEM serves as the basis for price regulation under the Drug Price Control Order (DPCO) administered by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA). Advocates are calling for inclusion of newer medicines for non-communicable diseases, anti-cancer drugs, and vaccines. The last major revision of the NLEM was in 2022.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (Health Governance); connects to NLEM, DPCO, NPPA, and India's pharmaceutical pricing and access to medicines policy.
key_facts: NLEM = National List of Essential Medicines
Regulated under Drug Price Control Order (DPCO) by NPPA
Last major revision: 2022
Demand: include newer drugs for NCDs, cancer, vaccines

title: Government Plans Cybersecurity Norms for Connected Vehicles Including Anti-Hijacking and OTA Update Rules
summary: The Government of India is planning to introduce regulations to address cybersecurity risks in increasingly connected and smart vehicles, including measures to prevent digital hijacking and standards for over-the-air (OTA) software updates. As modern vehicles incorporate internet connectivity and software-defined systems, they become vulnerable to cyberattacks. The proposed norms are being developed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. This initiative aligns with global regulatory trends for connected and autonomous vehicle security.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech and Infrastructure); connects to cybersecurity policy, connected vehicles, and India's evolving regulatory framework for emerging technologies.
key_facts: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to introduce connected vehicle cybersecurity norms
Covers anti-hijacking measures and OTA (over-the-air) software update standards
Addresses risks from smart/internet-connected vehicles
Aligns with global regulatory trends for autonomous and connected vehicles

title: Delhi Court Sentences BJP MLA Raju Kumar Singh to Four-Year Jail in Celebratory Firing Murder Case
summary: A Delhi court sentenced BJP MLA Raju Kumar Singh to four years of imprisonment in a celebratory firing murder case. The case involves death caused by celebratory gunfire, a recurring public safety concern in India. The conviction of a sitting Member of the Legislative Assembly is significant from the perspective of the Representation of the People Act, which deals with disqualification of elected representatives upon conviction. The sentence could trigger disqualification proceedings under Section 8 of the RPA, 1951.
exam_angle: Important for GS Paper 2 (Polity); connects to disqualification of elected representatives (Section 8, RPA 1951), elected officials' accountability, and criminal law.
key_facts: BJP MLA Raju Kumar Singh sentenced to 4 years imprisonment
Case: celebratory firing leading to murder in Delhi
Under RPA 1951 (Section 8), conviction with 2+ years triggers disqualification
Court: Delhi; significant for legislative accountability
